newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Fears of further falls in United States stocks caused Australian stock prices to fall by nearly two per cent yesterday, and prompted heavy selling on some of the world's main share markets, as brokers brace themselves for a further Wall Street fall today. Asian markets are especially feeling the drop, which comes in the wake of Japan's weak economy and turmoil over currencies in the region. Page 1.

Australian Taxation Office second commissioner Richard Highfield told the Senate economics committee yesterday that the ATO is about to begin a crackdown on salary sacrifice packages in a bid to recover the A$500 million the Federal Government had hoped to raise from a superannuation surcharge on high income earners. Page 1.

Federal Treasury Secretary Ted Evans told a Senate economics committee hearing that Australia has not been quick enough to adapt to changes in the global economy, and it must deregulate its labour market if wants to reduce unemployment. Last week however Prime Minister John Howard signalled the Federal Government would not consider further industrial relations reforms until after the next election. Page 1.

One year ago John Elliott and his colleagues were found not guilty of criminal proceedings in relation to Elders IXL. Tomorrow the Victorian Court of Appeal will hear an appeal over the legal reasoning of Judge Frank Vincent, who ruled the evidence in the case from the National Crime Authority inadmissible. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Fears of a global reaction to Friday's Wall Street fall saw the Australian all ordinaries drop 76 points in the first 30 minutes of trading yesterday to finish at 2618.5 points, down 47.7 points, as investors wiped A$7.3 billion from the share market. Page 1.

The latest Newspoll survey reveals that public support for a goods and services tax has reached 45 per cent, up from 27 per cent in June 1991. The result will give Prime Minister John Howard confidence as he attempts to sell widespread tax reform to Australian voters and begins seeking a mandate for this at the next federal election. Page 1.

The Federal Government's car industry tariff policy was endorsed by Toyota yesterday as the company committed A$1 billion to expand its Melbourne production centre and produce a new six-cylinder sedan to compete with the Commodore and Falcon. Page 1.

Federal Liberal backbencher Tony Smith has admitted paying for the services of a prostitute is wrong, after he was caught leaving a Brisbane brothel during a police raid. Smith has refused to resign from his position saying his conduct does not reflect upon his ability to work. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

New South Wales Teachers Federation analysis has revealed that popular private schools receive more government funding than public schools. This revelation has increased the calls for an end to government subsidies to private schools, with Federation presdent Denis Fitzgerald calling for an end to the systematic syphoning off of public school funds. Page 1.

At the launch of Barry Cohen's new book, From Whitlam to Winston, Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer attributed the loss of humour at Parliament House to the lack of communal toilets, saying private facilities prevented members from getting together. Page1

Federal Cabinet is split in its support for the ACT's proposed heroin trial after Federal Health Minister Michael Wooldridge admitted yesterday that the trial is unlikely to go ahead due to a lack of community support. The trial was originally endorsed by Wooldridge and State Health Ministers at a conference three weeks ago, but Prime Minister John Howard has been quite clear that he objects to the trial going ahead. Page 1.

While Australian stock prices fell heavily yesterday in the wake of the second-biggest Wall Street fall in history, the predicted hysteria didn't materialise after bargain hunters entered the market around noon, helping many stocks to recover. At the clos of trading the all ordinaries index had fallen 47.7 points to 2618.5. Page 1.
THE AGE

Car manufacturer Toyota has committed itself to investing up to A$1 billion in Victoria during the next seven years as part of its development of the new family sedan, the Avalon. Industry leaders believe the move by Toyota could create a large number of jobs in the Australian manufacturing industry. Page 1.

Four Treasury officials have been disciplined after a confidential document was obtained by the media. A Senate estimates committee has heard that the Treasury's international section head, Neil Hyden, had warned Treasury officials of the sensitivity and the need for security of the document about prominent Asia Pacific politicians. Page 1.

Victoria's TAFE Institutes have been given five weeks to respond to a Victorian Government review panel's recommendation that the State's 14 institutions be merged into no more than eight 'super TAFEs'. State Tertiary Education and Training Minister PhilHoneywood said the Government is not trying to close institutes, it just wants to ensure the widest range of courses are available to students. Page 1.

Australian golfer Karrie Webb, who took her first golf swing at the Ayr golf course, won her second women's British Open title with a record low score of 19-under 269 and a record-equalling eight-shot winning margin. Out of 18 United States PGA Tour tournments, Webb has finished in the top ten 15 times. Page 1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
